status_summary: The 2025 reconciliation law (Public Law 119-21, signed 2025-07-04) provides about $7.5 billion in Sec. 20001 for military quality of life, including an expansion of privatized military housing construction, per CRS. The FY2026 NDAA (Public Law 119-60, signed 2025-12-18) contains sections modifying the enlisted basic allowance for subsistence, increasing the family separation allowance (to $300 a month per Military Times), improving the basic allowance for housing and reviewing child care fee assistance limits, and a House member's release reports extension of the in-home child care pilot through 2029. Executive Order 14368 (signed 2025-12-18) set the uniformed services basic pay schedule effective 2026-01-01, which CRS lists as a 3.8 percent raise for all paygrades. A Department of War memo of 2026-04-01 told components to make maximum use of spouse employment flexibilities, and Executive Order 14417 (signed 2026-08-03) created a President's Military Spouse Commission to develop policies on housing, employment and other spouse concerns. No raise targeted at junior enlisted pay was enacted for 2026, and licensing reform appears in the order only as background.

timeline.event: Public Law 119-21 was enacted; its Sec. 20001 provides about $7.5 billion for military quality of life, including expanded privatized military housing construction (per CRS).

The President signed the FY2026 NDAA (S. 1071, Public Law 119-60); the Senate had agreed to the House amendment 77-20 on 2025-12-17. Its table of contents lists Sec. 621 (enlisted basic allowance for subsistence), Sec. 622 (family separation allowance increase), Sec. 624 (basic allowance for housing improvements) and Sec. 641 (child care fee assistance review). U.S. Code notes confirm that Sec. 621 rewrote the enlisted subsistence rate to follow the USDA monthly liberal food plan cost and that Sec. 622 raised the minimum monthly family separation allowance from $250 to $300.

Executive Order 14368, Adjustments of Certain Rates of Pay, set the 2026 monthly basic pay schedule for the uniformed services under 37 U.S.C. 203(a) as adjusted under 37 U.S.C. 1009, effective 2026-01-01; CRS lists the resulting raise as 3.8 percent for all paygrades.

The Under Secretary of War for Personnel and Readiness issued a memo directing fuller use of military spouse employment flexibilities, including a pilot letting spouses accept federal jobs before arriving at a new duty station.
Executive Order 14417 established the President's Military Spouse Commission to develop policies on housing, employment, health care, education and deployment support for military spouses.

title: Raise enlisted pay and allowances, improve housing, spouse jobs and childcare
uncertainties: Section text of Public Law 119-60 is not in the GovInfo HTML copy (the page holds only the table of contents and front matter), so section contents rest on section titles, a House member's release, Military Times and MOAA; the exact BAS mechanics and the BAH terms were not read. The 3.8 percent raise is the formula-based raise for all members; whether it counts as increasing wages in the Mandate's sense is a judgment call. A Marine Corps message reproduced on an unofficial mirror says the $300 family separation allowance applies retroactively to 2025-12-18; it was not used as a source. The FY2025 NDAA (Public Law 118-159) targeted junior enlisted raises predate the period. CRS does not break out child care or spouse items within Sec. 20001 of Public Law 119-21. The April 2026 memo was read only through MOAA. Spouse licensing and childcare capacity expansion were not found as new actions. The FY2027 request (7 percent for E-1 to E-5 per CRS) is not enacted. Pass 6 check: the BILLSTATUS record for S. 1071 confirms Public Law 119-60, signed 2025-12-18, after a 77-20 Senate vote on 2025-12-17. The GovInfo HTML of the law holds only the table of contents and the start of Division A within its first 128,000 characters, so Title VI text was not reached. U.S. Code editorial notes at law.cornell.edu confirm Sec. 621 (subsistence rate formula) and Sec. 622 (minimum family separation allowance $250 to $300, 37 U.S.C. 427). The note for 37 U.S.C. 403 cites only Sec. 611(e) of the law (extension of two temporary housing allowance provisions to 2026-12-31) and none for Sec. 624, so the Sec. 624 content and the Sec. 641 content remain based on section titles. The Federal Register API confirmed Executive Order 14417 (signed 2026-08-03, published 2026-08-06, 91 FR 51059). The 3.8 percent figure is taken from CRS IN12706 (Table 1), since the Executive Order 14368 pay schedule is an image not readable in the Federal Register page text; the order confirms the uniformed services schedule and its 2026-01-01 effective date. The FY2026 appropriation pay provisions were not read. Whether a FY2027 NDAA was enacted after CRS's 2026-07-14 status (House versions backing 7 percent for E-1 to E-5, Senate committee version 3.6 percent) was not checked.
